title: Prefill policy validator CLI and multi-quant preset labeller
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: prevent unit-econ regressions caused by incorrect prefill/batching defaults and mislabelled quantization presets. This PR introduces a lightweight CLI (prefill-policy-validator) for offline policy validation and a multi-quant preset labeller that attaches safety and econ metadata to quant profiles. Together these tools let platform and tenant engineers run deterministic checks during CI and as a manual dry-run before rolling out prefill/quant defaults.

What this PR does: - Adds cmd/prefill-validator: a small Go CLI that loads tenant prefill policy YAMLs and runs a rule-suite (cost, latency, compatibility) with explanatory diagnostics. - Adds scripts/quant_labeler: a Python utility that inspects quant preset artifacts and emits labeled JSON with safety tiers (strict, compatible, fallback) and an optional unit-econ score. - Integrates the validator into the CI pipeline as an optional check for the econ/ and deployment/ directories. - Adds docs and examples: docs/prefill-validator.md and examples/policies/sample-tenant-policy.yaml. - Adds e2e smoke tests and unit tests for the main validation rules.

Key capabilities: - Dry-run mode that reports potential cost regressions and incompatible quant profiles without failing builds (toggleable). - Tenant-aware checks: validator can run in tenant-mode to simulate tenant-specific constraints (GPU type, max-latency). - Label propagation: quant labeller annotates presets so serving can automatically pick safe fallbacks when a strict preset is unavailable. - Rule extensibility: rules live in pkg/prefill/rules.go and can be expanded; they include token-cost thresholds, cold-start penalty heuristics, and kv-cache usage assertions.

Checklist: - [x] CLI and labeller implemented - [x] Unit tests for validation rules - [x] E2E smoke test against a mini-simulated workload - [x] Documentation and quickstart - [x] CI integration (optional check gate)

Related work: Linked Linear tasks ENG-3421 (prefill policy safety harness) and ENG-3470 (quant preset metadata). This complements recent work on tenant warmstarts and batch templates (see ENG-3122).

Files changed (high level): see changed_files below for a concise list. The implementation is intentionally small and conservative: the validator reports issues by default and only fails pipelines when --fail-on-error is passed.

Testing and rollout: Ran e2e smoke locally and in CI. Initial rollout will enable the validator in dry-run mode for the econ/ and deployment/ directories for two weeks, followed by a staged enabling with --fail-on-error for infra and platform teams if no unexpected regressions are observed.

Followups: - Add a web endpoint to run the validator against a PR payload and attach results to PRs. - Extend the quant labeller to surface approximate inference-cost deltas per preset for common workloads.

review_comments: Jordan Li (reviewer): Please split the larger rule file into smaller rule modules — rules.go is getting crowded. Also add explicit examples of rule outputs so platform engineers can parse them.
Aisha Patel (author): Split rules.go into rules_cost.go and rules_compat.go in the follow-up commit; added sample output in docs/prefill-validator.md.
Marco Sørensen (reviewer): The quant labeller should tag presets with a lightweight compatibility fingerprint to avoid accidental application of strictly incompatible quant profiles.
Aisha Patel (author): Added 'compat_fingerprint' to the JSON schema emitted by the labeller; included tests to validate fingerprint uniqueness for test presets.
Priya Raman (approver): Verified e2e smoke against a small simulated tenant; leaving a single nit about log verbosity but approving for merge once addressed.
Aisha Patel (author): Reduced verbosity and switched noisy debug logs to --debug flag in final patch.
release_notes: Adds a prefilling policy validator CLI to detect potential cost and compatibility regressions before rollout. Adds a quant preset labeller that annotates quant artifacts with safety tiers and compatibility fingerprints. These tools are initially enabled as dry-run checks; platform owners can opt into failing-on-error after a monitoring window.
